message: No detected untrusted source handling: All data is loaded from local filesystem paths only; no remote source fetching (URLs, S3, HuggingFace Hub, etc.) is present, so no integrity verification or authentication is implemented.

No detected label flipping detection: The code logs label prevalence counts but performs no comparison against expected distributions, validation of label values against an expected set, or label-noise detection tools to catch flipped labels.

No detected data poisoning defenses: The data loading pipeline performs no outlier detection, statistical anomaly checks, or filtering of suspicious inputs on the training samples; it simply reads, resizes, and normalizes images.

No detected model integrity verification: Models are loaded via load_model() and keras applications without any hash check, signature verification, or pinned revision; no integrity verification is performed on pretrained weights or serialized checkpoints.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: No backdoor or trigger detection mechanisms such as neural cleanse, activation analysis, or gradient anomaly detection are present anywhere in the code.
No detected differential privacy: The code uses standard Adam optimizer and Keras training with no differential privacy library (Opacus, TensorFlow Privacy, DP-SGD) applied.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: No adversarial attack libraries (Foolbox, ART, etc.) or attack methods (FGSM, PGD) are imported or used anywhere in the evaluation code.

No detected metric tampering protection: While a train/test split exists in data.py, there is no held-out test set isolation enforcement, no hashing or signing of evaluation data, and only a single confusion matrix metric is reported without independent verification.

No detected input sanitization: The code only checks if the dataset path exists via check_if_exists_or_exit; there are no input shape, pixel range, or schema validation checks on images before passing them to the model.
No detected output bounds checks: Model predictions are consumed directly via np.argmax without any probability sanity checks, NaN guards, or confidence threshold validation.
No detected prompt injection defenses: This is a computer vision model (image classification), not an LLM, so prompt injection defenses are not applicable.
